newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Broker rates NAB, ANZ as buys.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Broker rates NAB, ANZ as buys.

text.p: Morgan Stockbroking Ltd recommended two of Australia's major banks as "buys" reflecting potential for solid growth in the leaders as well as opportunities for sector rationalisation.

In an overview of the sector, Morgan put buy recommendations on National Australia Bank Ltd and Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd as well as leading regional player, Bank of Western Australia Ltd.
Morgan also placed a buy recommendation on the newly-merged Suncorp-Metway-QIDC group while Westpac Banking Corp was recommended as a "hold."
"National Australia Bank is a sound portfolio stock with opportunities for further expansion," analyst Greg Cathro said in the report.
"(NAB) has the potential to surprise on the upside due to the geographic diversity of operations and the good track record," Cathro said.

ANZ was also a buy "offering reasonable fundamental value which could be enhanced further with cost savings and a higher dividend payout," he said. "Should rationalisation of the number of major banks proceed, then ANZ could be one which is subject to takeover speculation," Cathro said.

Cathro said Bank of Western Australia was a buy, based on growth in business lending and a focus on costs and fee income which should compensate for tight conditions in the West Australian home loan market.
The bank's growth in the second half of the current year to February 28, 1997 would be sourced from strength in business lending and capitalising on its local state franchise, Cathro said.

"Tough competition and recent housing interest rate reductions are expected to result in lower net interest margins in the second half," he said. "However higher earnings growth will be achieved through a focus on non-interest income intiiatives and reduced costs," he said.
Cathro rated Westpac a "hold" based on takeover speculation which was underpinning the share price.
"Speculation of a takeover is buoying the share price, despite a flat profit outlook and relatively full pricing relative to earnings and assets," Cathro said.
The Suncorp-Metway-QIDC group was a buy up to A$5.80, analyst Sophie Mitchell said.
"Metway Bank represents an investment in Queednsland's premier financial institution offering an attractive fully-franked yield with strong medium-term prospects," Mitchell said.
